title: Teen AI use separates instrumental help from emerging relational support
source_unit: US teen respondent, age 13-17, in Pew/Ipsos KnowledgePanel survey

denominator.unit: US teens ages 13-17 in completed Pew/Ipsos KnowledgePanel survey

observations.method: Pew Research Center online survey conducted through Ipsos KnowledgePanel; weighted to US teens ages 13-17 living with parents by age, gender, race and ethnicity, household income, and other categories.
observations.uncertainty: Purpose measures are self-reports with separate, non-exclusive question items. They do not measure session length, quality, dependence, clinical adequacy, privacy loss, or whether human support was displaced.
observations.subgroup: US teens ages 13-17; purpose-specific valid response universes are retained by the source.
observations.counterinterpretation: Information and schoolwork use may be instrumental and reversible, while conversational or emotional-support use may still be occasional and not a durable relationship.

related_sources.claim: Pew reports teen chatbot purposes, including information, schoolwork, conversation, and emotional support.
Pew documents the survey design and teen respondent methodology.

boundary: This record separates instrumental and relational teen chatbot use in a population survey. It does not establish emotional dependence, learning gains, mental-health effects, human-support substitution, platform manipulation, privacy loss, trust change, or practical exit.
